body.statement: There is an explicit computable \(C_{\mathrm{map}}\) such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), uniformly over \((P_n)\in\mathcal M(J,K,\mathcal H,\mathcal K_V)\), \(d_{\mathrm{BL}}\{\mathcal L(T_n),\mathcal L(G(h,Z_{V_n}))\}\le\varepsilon_n\) in \(C([0,1])\), with \(\varepsilon_n\) given in \(\mathrm{def:curve\mbox{-}rate}\) and \(\varepsilon_n\to0\). The same coupling is joint with \(E_n\), and the bound includes both compactified endpoints.
body.justification: A quantitative function-valued law is the inferential object needed when the KL weight is selected after observing the sample-computable plug-in frontier.
body.gap: Fang--Ridder--Xie is pointwise at each fixed positive penalty and separate at the deterministic boundary; Whitehouse et al. use one predetermined diverging smoother for a different scalar target.
body.consumer: Together with the operational-selector bridge, it permits simultaneous regret inference at every temperature chosen measurably from the observed sample or its plug-in frontier.
body.proof_tex:
Write
\[
 H_0=\sup_{h\in\mathcal H}\|h\|_\infty<\infty,\qquad
 x_n=\sqrt{r_n}+\rho_n .
\]
We first turn the bounded-Lipschitz bound into a coupling without imposing
any new assumption.  For a closed set \(A\) and \(\delta\in(0,1]\), the
ramp \(x\mapsto(1-\operatorname{dist}(x,A)/\delta)_+\) is bounded by one
and has Lipschitz constant \(\delta^{-1}\).  Therefore
\[
 P(E_n\in A)\le P(Z_{V_n}\in A^\delta)+r_n/\delta .
\]
With \(\delta=\sqrt{r_n}\), the same inequality with the two laws
interchanged gives the defining inequalities for Prokhorov distance
\(\sqrt{r_n}\).  Approximating both laws by finite rational partitions and
applying the finite marriage lemma, then taking a tight subsequential limit,
constructs a coupling satisfying
\[
 P\{\|E_n-Z_{V_n}\|_\infty>\sqrt{r_n}\}\le\sqrt{r_n}.                  \tag{32}
\]
This construction is the elementary proof of the coupling implication; it
does not add an assumption to the model.

Fix \(M\ge1\) and \(0<a\le1/4\) with \(x_n\le a/8\).  Let
\(\mathcal B(M,a)\) be the event on which (32) succeeds,
\(\|Z_{V_n}\|_\infty\le M\), and every within-stratum pairwise coordinate
gap of \(R(h+Z_{V_n})\) exceeds \(a\).  The Gaussian coordinate tail bound
and (24) give
\[
 P\{\mathcal B(M,a)^c\}
 \le\sqrt{r_n}
 +2d e^{-M^2/(2v_{\max})}
 +{JK(K-1)a\over\sqrt{2\pi v_{\min}}}.                               \tag{33}
\]
On this event,
\[
 \|u_n-h\|_\infty\le\rho_n,\qquad
 \|E_n-Z_{V_n}\|_\infty\le\sqrt{r_n},
\]
so every hard winning action is unchanged when
\((h,Z_{V_n})\) is replaced by \((u_n,E_n)\).

For completeness, we derive the deterministic path modulus used on
\(\mathcal B(M,a)\).  Put
\[
 c_0={a\over8\log\{\exp(1)+M/a\}}.
\]
For \(0<c\le c_0\), apply (23) to both paths.  Their common hard profile,
the two-Lipschitz dependence of the hard loss on its first argument, and
\(\exp(-a/(2c))\le\{a/(\exp(1)+M/a)\}^4\) yield
\[
 \sup_{0<c\le c_0}
 |(1+c)L_c(u_n,E_n)-(1+c)L_c(h,Z_{V_n})|
 \le C_0\{Ma+x_n\},                                                   \tag{34}
\]
where \(L_c(u,z)=\sum_jp_j\ell_{c,b_j}(Ru_j,Rz_j)\) and
\[
 C_0=2^8JK^2\beta^{-2}(1+H_0).
\]
For \(c\ge c_0\), differentiate the integral representation (11) in both
arguments.  The identities
\[
 Dq_{c,b}(v)={1\over c}C\{q_{c,b}(v)\},\qquad
 \|C(r)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le1,
\]
together with (17)--(18), give, along the segment joining the two input
pairs,
\[
 \sup_{c\ge c_0}
 |(1+c)L_c(u_n,E_n)-(1+c)L_c(h,Z_{V_n})|
 \le C_1\,{x_n(1+M)^2
 \log\{\exp(1)+M/a\}\over a},                                        \tag{35}
\]
where one admissible explicit value is
\[
 C_1=2^{10}JK^2\beta^{-2}(1+H_0)(1+v_{\max}+v_{\min}^{-1}).
\]
For \(c\ge1/c_0\), the apparent factor \(c\) in this differentiation is
cancelled by subtracting the quadratic endpoint and using (19); this is why
the right side of (35), rather than a bound growing with \(c\), holds.
The same calculations at \(c=0\) and \(c=\infty\) prove that (34)--(35)
include both compactified endpoints.  Combining them and enlarging the
constant gives
\[
 \|G(u_n,E_n)-G(h,Z_{V_n})\|_\infty
 \le C_2\left[
 Ma+{x_n(1+M)^2\log\{\exp(1)+M/a\}\over a}\right]                     \tag{36}
\]
on \(\mathcal B(M,a)\), with
\[
 C_2=2^{12}JK^2\beta^{-2}p_{\min}^{-1}
 (1+H_0)^2(1+v_{\max}+v_{\min}^{-1}).
\]

Let \(F\) be bounded by one and one-Lipschitz for the bounded supremum norm
on \(C([0,1])\).  On \(\mathcal B(M,a)\), use (36); on its complement use
\(|F|\le1\).  Equations (33)--(36) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left|E F\{G(u_n,E_n)\}-E F\{G(h,Z_{V_n})\}\right|\\
 &\quad\le C_{\mathrm{map}}\left[
 \sqrt{r_n}+{JK^2a\over\sqrt{v_{\min}}}
 +d e^{-M^2/(2v_{\max})}+Ma
 +{x_n(1+M)^2\log\{\exp(1)+M/a\}\over a}\right],                      \tag{37}
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the explicit computable choice
\[
 C_{\mathrm{map}}
 =2^{14}JK^2\beta^{-2}p_{\min}^{-1}
 (1+H_0)^2(1+v_{\max}+v_{\min}^{-1})
\]
dominates every numerical constant above.  Taking the displayed infimum in
\(\mathrm{def:curve\mbox{-}rate}\) proves the asserted uniform
bounded-Lipschitz inequality.

It remains to check the limit.  Because \(r_n=C_{\mathrm{BE}}n^{-1/2}\)
and \(\rho_n\downarrow0\), \(x_n\downarrow0\).  For example, set
\[
 a_n=x_n^{1/3},\qquad
 M_n=\max\{1,\sqrt{2v_{\max}\log(1/x_n)}\}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), the constraint \(x_n\le a_n/8\) holds.
Every term in the bracket in (37) then tends to zero; the last is
\(O\{x_n^{2/3}\log^2(1/x_n)\}\).  Hence \(\varepsilon_n\to0\).
Finally, (32) is a coupling of \(E_n\) and \(Z_{V_n}\) itself, and all
path comparisons were made on that same probability space.  Thus (37)
also holds for the joint pairs
\((T_n,E_n)\) and \((G(h,Z_{V_n}),Z_{V_n})\) under the corresponding
bounded product norm, which proves the asserted joint version.
